title: Pin-triggered synthetic scan + priority fanout for preflight evals
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a two-stage, cost-aware automated evaluation pipeline that fires when a model version is pinned (catalog or tenant-pinned). This ticket defines a lightweight 'synthetic scan' preflight that runs immediately and a prioritized fanout for deeper/full evals. The design must minimize cost and latency impact, give a deterministic safety signal for immediate rollback decisions, and produce observability in the Console for operators and customers.

Motivation: Current post-pin evals are heavy and either delayed or expensive. We need a fast safety gate for critical regressions and a queueing strategy to backfill deeper evaluations without overwhelming capacity or costing the tenant/shipping team unexpectedly.

Key behaviors: 
- Trigger point: model-version pin event (catalog change or customer pin). Hook lives in the pin-authoring service; an event payload contains model_id, version, change_id, actor, scope (catalog|tenant), and pin_reason.
- Stage 1 (synthetic scan): run a small, curated prompt set (5–20 items, tenant-specific or catalog baseline) across the new model variant. This should be lightweight (<30s wall time typical) and produce a pass/fail signal plus delta metrics (quality_score_delta, avg_latency, top-1-regressions). The synthetic scan must run synchronously enough to inform an immediate canary fallback policy (fail-fast threshold).
- Stage 2 (priority fanout): if synthetic scan passes or is inconclusive, enqueue deeper evals into priority lanes: "fast-lane" (automated smoke suite, medium sample), "standard-lane" (full catalog/tenant eval), "deep-lane" (long-running thorough suites for high-risk tenants). Lanes are prioritized by scope, customer tier, and explicit pin priority.
- Cost controls: per-pin cost caps, tenant-specified budget, global staging budget, and dynamic sampling to keep within a monthly compute allowance. If budget exhausted, deep-lane evals are delayed and a console notice is posted.
- Sampling & prioritization: For catalog-wide pins, run synthetic scan universally, but deep-lane evals sample tenants using a stratified approach (high-usage + random sample + opt-in test tenants). For tenant-pins, run full tenant-scoped evals immediately if tenant is enterprise or has opted into full-evals; otherwise default to synthetic + scheduled standard-lane.
- Observability & alerts: Synthetic scan results push to the Console as a preflight card with delta metrics and an auto-generated human-readable summary. If delta_quality < -X% or regression_count >= Y, trigger high-severity alert and optionally block activation. All steps emit traces and link to the pin change event, PR, and evaluation artifacts.
- Rollback behavior: If the synthetic scan breaches thresholds, the pin authoring system should automatically mark the pin as blocked and initiate an automatic rollback/fallback to previous model variant for serving routes that subscribed to fail-fast. A manual override by a product engineer must be auditable.
- Dry-run & opt-in: provide a dry-run mode (no service interruptions) and an admin opt-out for early adopters. There should also be an "opt-into-full-evals" toggle per-customer.
- Integration points: pin service (trigger), eval-orchestrator (pipeline), exec workers (synthetic runner), Console (UI), billing (cost delta reporting), telemetry (datadog/prometheus), alerting (PagerDuty/Slack).

Non-functional requirements: 
- Synthetic scan median p95 completion < 45s.
- System must respect tenant budget and not exceed per-pin cost cap by more than 5%.
- All eval artifacts must be stored for 90 days and have immutable links in the Console preflight card.

Acceptance criteria (see field below) and an initial roll-out plan are in comments. Implementation will require collaboration with ENG (eval runtime, orchestration), Security (KMS/audit on artifacts), and Billing.

Notes on uniqueness vs existing work: unlike previous designs that focused on triggering full evals or long-running canaries, this ticket emphasizes a fast synthetic gate plus priority-driven fanout and explicit cost controls to reduce noise and unexpected billing while preserving safety for tenant and catalog changes.
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic scan executes automatically on every pin event and returns a pass/inconclusive/fail signal within 45s p95.
Console shows a preflight card for each pin with a human-readable summary, delta_quality, and a link to full artifacts.
Fail-fast rollback is performed when synthetic scan meets defined regression thresholds; rollback events are auditable.
Priority fanout enqueues deeper evals into fast/standard/deep lanes with stratified tenant sampling for catalog pins.
Per-pin cost caps and tenant budgets are enforced; deep-lane evals do not run if budget would be exceeded without explicit approval.
Telemetry (trace id from pin -> eval artifacts) exists and key metrics (quality_delta, latency, token_count, regression_count) are visible in runtime dashboards.
Security review completed and artifacts stored with tenant-level access control and KMS encryption.
comments: 2026-01-15 Aisha Patel: Initial write-up and scope. Put high emphasis on short synthetic scan to reduce noisy false positives and cost. Created this ticket to align PM/ENG/Console work.

2026-01-20 Diego Ramos: Eng intake — scoped synthetic runner + small prompt set. We need a mapping table for tenant prompt profiles vs catalog baseline. Opening ENG spike to estimate execution cost (ENG-62177).
2026-01-22 Priya Malhotra (Design): Shared mockups for Console preflight card and an inline \"approve/override\" button. Link: https://confluence.redwoodinference/display/EVALS/Pin+Preflight+Card

2026-01-27 Ben Carter (SRE): Raised capacity concern — synthetic scans at scale could burst workers during large catalog pin. Proposal: rate-limit triggers and use token bucket by catalog_release window.

2026-01-30 Diego Ramos: Decision log — implement two-phase pipeline. Synthetic runner runs on a lightweight sku, returns structured JSON with metrics. Fanout orchestrator enqueues lanes with cost-aware throttling. PR for orchestrator shim: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-orchestrator/pull/278
2026-02-02 Liu Zhang (Security): Security review flagged artifact storage encryption and audit trail requirements. Marking security_review_required=true and adding KMS integration task for ENG-62234.
2026-02-03 Aisha Patel: Updated acceptance thresholds and added rollout plan: alpha internal tenants (2 weeks) -> beta customers (opt-in, 4 weeks) -> default-on for catalog pins after metrics stable.
release_notes: Adds a lightweight preflight synthetic scan on model pin events and a prioritized eval fanout with cost controls. Initial rollout is alpha internal -> opt-in beta -> default for catalog pins.
